channel.title: Saindani
channel.description: Posts on finance, technology, and behaviour from a former banking regulator (RBI, BNP Paribas, Nasdaq) turned fintech founder.

item.title: The Age of Specialisation Is Over
item.description: For a century, going deeper meant getting ahead. AI is dissolving the scarcity that made narrow expertise pay.

item.title: Your Brain Works Like ChatGPT. That Should Unsettle You.
item.description: Neuroscience's predictive processing model says your brain isn't reacting to the world, it's constantly guessing what comes next and correcting itself when wrong.

item.title: Money Is Breaking in Slow Motion
item.description: No single asset in 2025-2026 managed to store value, enable exchange, and price things reliably at the same time. That's a design flaw, not an accident.

item.title: The Compliance Department Exists to Be Blamed
item.description: It has no authority to stop anything and full accountability when something goes wrong.

item.title: Passive Investing Only Works Because Most People Won't Do It
item.description: Index funds beat active managers for a reason most evangelists never mention: the strategy depends on staying a minority position.

item.title: The Algorithm Didn't Radicalize You. Engagement Did.
item.description: Blaming the code lets everyone skip the harder question: what does it say about us that outrage is what we reward?

item.title: Emergency Funds Are a Confidence Trick You Play on Yourself
item.description: The 3-6 months rule was never really about math. It's a psychological hedge dressed up as one.

item.title: Central Banks Can't Rescue You From Your Landlord
item.description: Rate cuts move the price of buying assets, not the cost of using them. Your rent is a local supply fight, not a monetary one.

item.title: Your Startup Isn't Disrupting Anything. It's Just Skipping the Paperwork.
item.description: Half of fintech's "disruption" is regulatory arbitrage with better branding. Here's how to tell the difference.
